# Add a vignette

- Route: `/tools/add-vignette`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `photo`
- Slug: `add-vignette`

## Summary

Darken or lighten the edges of a photo with midpoint, roundness, feather and highlight protection. (Photo editing)

## Details

The Vignette section of the Aperture Detail panel multiplies each pixel by a factor that depends on how far it sits from the center of the frame. Amount runs from -100 to 100: negative values darken the edges for the classic drawing-the-eye-inward look, positive values brighten them, which is how you cancel the natural fall-off of a wide-open lens. Midpoint sets where the effect begins, Feather how gradually it ramps, Roundness whether the shape follows the rectangular frame or a circle, and Highlights protects bright pixels from being darkened. It is a detail layer like any other, so it can be masked, faded with opacity and undone. The preview on your GPU and the server export use the same distance metric and the same smoothstep ramp.
### What it does
- Darkens the edges with a negative Amount or lightens them with a positive one, multiplying each pixel by 1 + amount/100 times the frame distance factor.
- Starts the effect at the Midpoint and ramps it over the Feather width with a smoothstep, so there is never a visible ring.
- Shapes the fall-off with Roundness: -100 follows the rectangle of the frame, 0 is halfway, 100 is a true circle centered on the frame that reaches the four corners.
- Protects bright pixels when darkening: with Highlights at 50, a pixel at luma 0.9 is darkened only 55 percent as much as a black one.
- Exports from the original at full resolution with the normalized frame coordinates, so the vignette lands in the same place on the 24 MP file as on the preview.
### How to use it
1. Open the photo: Drop a JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC or other photo; the Detail panel opens with the Vignette sliders visible.
2. Choose a direction: Drag Amount to about -30 for a subtle darkening or to +20 to +40 to lift corners that a lens has darkened.
3. Shape it: Lower Midpoint to pull the effect inward, raise Feather to soften the transition, and set Roundness to 100 for a circular shape on a wide frame.
4. Protect and export: Raise Highlights so bright skies keep their brightness, check with the backslash key, then export JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF or TIFF.
### Supported formats
- Input: JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, HEIC, HEIF, AVIF, TIFF, BMP
- Output: JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, TIFF
- The vignette is computed in normalized frame coordinates, so it is identical at any export size from 12 to 120 megapixels.
- PNG exports keep transparency; a transparent corner left by a rotation is multiplied like any other pixel but stays transparent.
### Technical details
- Each pixel gets normalized coordinates nx and ny from -1 to 1 across the frame (pixel centers at +0.5). Two distances are computed: the rectangle metric max(|nx|, |ny|), and the circle metric, the Euclidean distance from the center in pixels divided by the half diagonal. They are blended with weight (roundness + 100)/200 on the circle, so Roundness -100 is pure rectangle, 0 is a 50/50 mix and 100 is pure circle. Every metric is 0 at the center and exactly 1 at the four corners.
- The factor v is smoothstep(midpoint/100, midpoint/100 + feather/100, d): 0 until the distance reaches the midpoint, 1 once it reaches midpoint plus feather, with the cubic 3t squared minus 2t cubed ease between. At the defaults Midpoint 50 and Feather 50, a pixel halfway to a corner has v = 0, a pixel three quarters of the way has v = 0.5, and a pixel at d = 0.9 has v = 0.896.
- The pixel is multiplied by k = 1 + amount/100 times v times prot, where prot = 1 - highlights/100 times the BT.709 luma of the pixel when Amount is negative and 1 when it is positive, then clamped to 0..1. Lightening therefore clips: with Amount +30 at a corner, a pixel at 0.8 (204) becomes 1.0 (255).
- On a 6000 x 4000 frame with Roundness 0 the middle of a short side is at d = 0.916 and the middle of a long edge at d = 0.777; with Roundness 100 those become 0.832 and 0.555, so a circular vignette leaves the top and bottom edges noticeably lighter than the sides on a 3:2 frame.
- The Aperture preview is drawn on your GPU (WebGL2) from a 1920 px copy, the export is rendered on our server from the original at full resolution with the same formulas, and the two agree within a small documented tolerance; for the vignette that is a mean error of at most one 8-bit level, since the distance is computed in normalized frame units and does not depend on the pixel count.
### When not to use it
Skip the vignette when the subject is at the edge of the frame, since any centered darkening will dim it; use a Local adjustment with a radial mask placed over the subject instead. Do not use a positive Amount to brighten a whole underexposed photo: it only lifts the corners and clips bright pixels at 255, while the Exposure slider raises everything evenly. For a solid border or a frame around the picture, a vignette is the wrong tool altogether because its ramp is always soft; crop to the aspect you want and add the border in a layout program.
### Use cases
- Portraits against a busy background: Amount -35, Midpoint 40, Feather 60, Roundness 60 pulls attention to the face without an obvious dark ring.
- Correcting a wide-open 35mm lens: Amount +25, Midpoint 30, Feather 70, Roundness 100 raises the corner values by up to 25 percent and evens the sky.
- Product shots on white: A slight negative vignette with Highlights 80 keeps the white backdrop white while subtly grounding the object.
- Square social crops: Set the crop first in Geometry; the vignette is computed on the cropped frame, so the corners stay in the corners.
### FAQ
Q: How do I remove the vignette a lens left in my photo?
A: Use a positive Amount. Lens fall-off is roughly circular and reaches the corners, so Roundness 100, Midpoint 20 to 35 and Feather 60 to 80 with Amount +15 to +40 usually cancels it. Watch bright corners, since lightening clips at 255.
Q: Why does the vignette look round on the preview but reach the sides first on export?
A: It does not; the distance is normalized to the frame on both. What changes the shape is Roundness: at -100 it follows the rectangle and the side edges darken first, at 100 it is a circle centered on the frame.
Q: What does Highlights do exactly?
A: When Amount is negative, the darkening of each pixel is scaled by 1 - highlights/100 times its luma. At Highlights 100 a pure white pixel is not darkened at all and a mid-gray is darkened half as much. It has no effect when Amount is positive.
Q: Does the vignette follow the crop?
A: Yes. Geometry, including crop and straighten, is applied before any layer, so the center and corners are those of the cropped frame, not of the original file.
Q: Can I make the vignette off-center?
A: Not with the vignette sliders, which are always centered. For an off-center darkening, add a Local adjustment with a Radial mask, invert it and lower Exposure; the radial mask has a draggable center, size and rotation.
Q: Will a dark vignette shift colors in the corners?
A: The multiplication scales R, G and B equally, so hue is unchanged, though a dark corner can look slightly more saturated. Set the layer blend to Luminosity if you want the chroma left exactly as it was.

## Routing

When to send a visitor here: Use when someone wants to darken or lighten the edges of a photo to draw the eye to the centre, with midpoint, roundness, feather and highlight protection. Typical asks: "add a vignette", "darken the corners".
When to send them elsewhere: If the subject sits at the frame edge, a vignette will dim it; use a radial mask in Aperture (aperture). To brighten a whole dark photo use Fix exposure (fix-photo-exposure). It cannot add a solid border.
Related tools: fix-photo-exposure (brighten the whole photo); black-and-white-photo (pairs with monochrome); split-toning (finishing colour grade); crop-image (reframe before vignetting)
